title: Cocartesian criterion for finite-product cartesian envelopes
statement:
Use infinity categories, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and cartesian symmetric monoidal envelopes over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Let $p:E\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration of infinity categories with finite products. Suppose $p$ preserves finite products, including the terminal object, and the product of two $p$-cocartesian edges is $p$-cocartesian. Then $p^\times:E^\times\to B^\times$ is a cocartesian fibration. For a pointed map $\alpha:\langle r\rangle\to\langle s\rangle$, block arrows $b_j:\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}p(e_i)\to b'_j$ in $B$ and a tuple $(e_i)$, a $p^\times$-cocartesian lift is given by the block arrows
$$\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i\longrightarrow (b_j)_!\left(\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i\right),$$
where $(b_j)_!$ denotes $p$-cocartesian transport. An edge over this tuple arrow is $p^\times$-cocartesian if and only if all its block arrows in $E$ are $p$-cocartesian. Empty blocks use the terminal object of $E$. These statements and lift descriptions remain valid after pullback along the ordered-block functor $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. This functor assigns to $a:[s]\to[r]$ the blocks $\{a(j-1)+1,\ldots,a(j)\}$ and discards all remaining inputs. All categories fit in containing universes.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng Corollary 6.8 and Proposition 6.7(ii); block mapping criterion from their proof, specialized to cartesian envelopes. Online source read; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag.

proof.text:
Use the intrinsic mapping-space convention for cocartesian functors in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], which also supplies a simplicial cocartesian representative after replacement over the base. The finite-product-preserving functor $p$ induces the coherent functor $P=p^\times$ by [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. For an edge $u:x=(e_i)_{i=1}^r\to y=(f_j)_{j=1}^s$ over $\alpha$, put $x_j=\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i$ and write its blocks as $u_j:x_j\to f_j$. Identify $p(x_j)$ with $\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}p(e_i)$ by the specified product comparison. For a test tuple $z=(z_k)_{k=1}^t$ the envelope formula gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E^\times}(y,z)\simeq\coprod_{\beta:\langle s\rangle\to\langle t\rangle}\prod_{k=1}^t\operatorname{Map}_E\!\left(\prod_{\beta(j)=k}f_j,z_k\right).$$
Indeed a right-pinched simplex maps to a simplex in the nerve of $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ with constant initial face, hence has one fixed pointed-map label; this partitions the mapping space degreewise. The same applies to $x$ and to $B^\times$. Composition takes the label $\beta$ to $\beta\alpha$ and uses the block-substitution formula of the cited envelope node. All formulas are natural equivalences of spaces with their composition maps.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text: The binary product hypothesis implies closure of $p$-cocartesian edges under every nonempty finite product: for a singleton there is nothing to prove, and adjoining one factor is exactly the binary hypothesis. The nullary product of arrows is $\mathrm{id}_{1_E}$; its precomposition square has horizontal identities, so it is cocartesian by the intrinsic criterion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Thus this closure includes empty products without assuming that every arrow from a terminal object is cocartesian. Changing a product cone by its projection-preserving equivalence changes the mapping-space squares by equivalences and therefore does not change their pullback property.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text:
Suppose all $u_j$ are $p$-cocartesian. Fix a pointed map $\beta:\langle s\rangle\to\langle t\rangle$ and put $J_k=\{j:\beta(j)=k\}$, $a_k=\prod_{j\in J_k}x_j$, $c_k=\prod_{j\in J_k}f_j$, and $v_k=\prod_{j\in J_k}u_j:a_k\to c_k$. Step 2 makes every $v_k$ cocartesian, including $v_k=\mathrm{id}_{1_E}$ if $J_k$ is empty. Regrouping the disjoint input blocks identifies $a_k\simeq\prod_{\beta\alpha(i)=k}e_i$. The intrinsic criterion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] therefore gives, for each $k$, the homotopy-pullback square
$$\begin{matrix}\operatorname{Map}_E(c_k,z_k)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_E(a_k,z_k)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \operatorname{Map}_B(p(c_k),p(z_k))&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(a_k),p(z_k)).\end{matrix}$$
Taking the finite product of these squares gives the square on the $\beta$-part of the envelope cocartesian test: [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] identifies its top map with precomposition by $u$, and likewise in $B$. This finite-product assertion follows directly in the path-pullback model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: a path in a product is a tuple of paths, so the path pullback of product maps is the product of their path pullbacks, and the product of the comparison equivalences has the product of their inverses. It also holds for $t=0$.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text:
Assemble the squares of step 3 over all $\beta$. In the total path pullback
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E^\times}(x,z)\mathbin{\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{B^\times}(Px,Pz)}}\operatorname{Map}_{B^\times}(Py,Pz),$$
a point of the second factor has a label $\beta$. A path identifying its composite with $P(u)$ to the image of a point of the first factor forces that first point to have label $\beta\alpha$, since the pointed-map labels are discrete. Thus this pullback is the coproduct over $\beta$ of precisely the path pullbacks in step 3. The upper-left space $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\times}(y,z)$ has the same decomposition by step 1. The comparison is consequently a coproduct of equivalences, with inverses defined on the same summands, and is an equivalence. This proves the total cocartesian square for every tuple $z$, hence $u$ is $P$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. No injectivity of $\beta\mapsto\beta\alpha$ is needed: distinct $\beta$ remain distinct summands in the second factor.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $u$ is $P$-cocartesian. For each $j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and each $z\in E$, test its intrinsic square on the one-term tuple $(z)$ and restrict the lower-left mapping space to the summand labeled by the inert projection $\rho_j:\langle s\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ selecting $j$. The path-pullback description and the discrete labels of step 1 restrict the upper-left space to that same label and the upper-right space to label $\rho_j\alpha$. The envelope formula identifies the resulting square with
$$\begin{matrix}\operatorname{Map}_E(f_j,z)&\xrightarrow{\circ u_j}&\operatorname{Map}_E(x_j,z)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \operatorname{Map}_B(p(f_j),p(z))&\xrightarrow{\circ p(u_j)}&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x_j),p(z)).\end{matrix}$$
Restricting a pullback to a union of these discrete summands is again a pullback: its path model simply retains those summands and the inverse comparison restricts to them. The square is therefore a homotopy pullback for every $z$, so $u_j$ is $p$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. When $s=0$ there is no condition; step 4 already proves every edge to the empty tuple cocartesian.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text: Given $(e_i)$ and a base tuple arrow with blocks $b_j$, use the cocartesian lifting property of $p$ on the object $x_j=\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}e_i$ and on the arrow $p(x_j)\simeq\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}p(e_i)\xrightarrow{b_j}b'_j$. It gives $u_j:x_j\to(b_j)_!x_j$ over that arrow. The coherent envelope mapping formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] realizes this tuple of blocks as an edge over the given tuple arrow (retaining its specified identification in the base). Steps 3-4 prove it $P$-cocartesian. Every object and every outgoing base arrow admit this construction, so $P$ is a cocartesian fibration in the intrinsic convention of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]; its comparison with the simplicial convention supplies the corresponding representative. All higher coherences already belong to the functor $p^\times$ constructed in the envelope node; this argument proves a property of its arrows rather than attempting to reconstruct a functor from binary operations. Empty $\alpha$-blocks use $x_j=1_E$ and $p(1_E)\simeq1_B$, so the lifting property applies there as well.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Free algebras through Day convolution, Proposition 6.7(ii) and Corollary 6.8, printed pp. 14-15; direct verification using the existing cartesian-envelope mapping formula.

proof.text: Define $F:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$ by $F([r])=\langle r\rangle$ and $F(a^{\mathrm{op}})(i)=j$ when $a(j-1)<i\leq a(j)$, and $*$ otherwise. The intervals are disjoint. Identities give singleton intervals. For $a:[s]\to[r]$ and $b:[t]\to[s]$, the consecutive union of intervals indexed by $b(k-1)<j\leq b(k)$ is exactly $\{a(b(k-1))+1,\ldots,a(b(k))\}$, including the empty case. Thus $F(a^{\mathrm{op}})$ followed by $F(b^{\mathrm{op}})$ equals $F((a\circ b)^{\mathrm{op}})$, including every discarded index. This proves it is a functor; its nerve retains all chains and their face and degeneracy maps. For $[0]$, the tuple is empty, and a constant $a$ produces empty output blocks.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng Example 3.2, printed p. 5; explicit ordered-block composition verification.

proof.text: Put $E_F=E^\times\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and define $B_F$ similarly, using infinity-categorical pullbacks. Then $E_F\simeq E^\times\times_{B^\times}B_F$ by the defining data of these pullbacks. Base-change compatibility of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] shows $E_F\to B_F$ is cocartesian and its transports are the same transports over the image arrows in $B^\times$. In particular step 6 supplies lifts with exactly the stated interval blocks. For completeness the entire block criterion, including necessity, can be checked without assuming reflection of cocartesian arrows under an arbitrary functor: repeat steps 1-5 with labels the ordinal maps instead of pointed maps. The mapping spaces are now decomposed over the discrete hom sets of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and composition is the same block substitution by step 7 and [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Sufficiency uses the same finite products $v_k$. For necessity, the opposite of $[1]\to[s]$, $0\mapsto j-1$, $1\mapsto j$, selects the singleton block $j$, so the test in step 5 again gives exactly the square for $u_j$. Thus an edge of the pullback is cocartesian exactly when its blocks are $p$-cocartesian, including nullary blocks and discarded end intervals.
